solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Member of the unprivileged classes needs a following — now's the time

parts.note: a commoner is someone not of the nobility or privileged ranks

explanation.surface: A social commentator says the lower orders need a following, and the moment is now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs a following' means the letter A comes after. The Common Era is the dating system for years since AD 1, the period we are living in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the present calendar epoch, so it names the age we are in today.

clue.text: Clue to all the workers' unions being distressed

parts.note: the Trades Union Congress (TUC) is the federation of all Britain's workers' unions; the answer, read as an instruction in a down entry, spells those three initials going upward

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint about the union federation, which is in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a clue: CUT going up (in a down entry) gives TUC, the Trades Union Congress, Britain's national federation of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut up is to be upset or deeply hurt, an informal British idiom for distressed.

clue.text: Fellow holding dance, not half, upset one of two bands?

indicators.note: holding says the fellow goes around the upturned dance

parts.note: a male is a man or fellow

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the shortened dance is turned upside down
not half says only the first part of the dance's name is kept

parts.note: the cancan is a high-kicking dance

explanation.surface: A man clutching a dancer, half-turned upside down, wears one of two wristbands.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means written bottom to top. The '?' flags that the definition is cryptic: handcuffs come in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs come as a pair of shackles, so one fetter is one of two bands round the wrists.

clue.text: Communication shared with the public exposed character

parts.note: open means exposed or uncovered
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A public message lays bare someone's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter addressed to a person but published so everyone can read it is a public message.

clue.text: No longer last? Jump for joy

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
ult is short for ultimo, last month

explanation.surface: No longer in last place, you leap with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice triumphantly, the feeling behind leaping for joy.

clue.text: Sign impedes worker in the East End

indicators.note: in the East End says both words are said Cockney-style, losing their initial aitch

parts.note: hampers means impedes
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A sign blocks a labourer in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys of London's East End traditionally drop their aitches, so HAMPERS and HAND lose their H.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the typographical symbol for 'and', so it is a written sign.

clue.text: Bit of land needing order, wicked place

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A plot of ground needs tidying, in a place of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, is a British order of distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed for its sinfulness is the byword for a den of iniquity.

clue.text: Unhappy note — and another

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
re is another sol-fa note

explanation.surface: A sad note is followed by a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore can mean aggrieved or upset, as in 'feeling sore about it'.

clue.text: Duke with posh car becomes more whimsical

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A duke with a luxury car becomes more fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means quaintly amusing, so the comparative is more comically odd.

clue.text: Stingy person keeps material on roof, not one to be trusted

indicators.note: keeps says the stingy person holds the roofing metal inside

parts.note: a miser hoards money
lead sheeting is used on roofs

explanation.surface: A tightwad stores roofing material and is not to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads others astray deceives them, so cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: Sort of cover one aunt knitted

indicators.note: knitting works the yarn into a new pattern, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt knits a cosy of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A tonneau cover is the fitted canvas sheet stretched over the open back of a pickup or an open car's seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is a type of fitted protective sheet for an open vehicle, so it is one kind of covering.

clue.text: Dreadful rooms one of the two kings abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned says the king is left out of the rooms

parts.note: parlours are sitting rooms
chess and card notation give K and R (Rex) for king; R is one of the pair

explanation.surface: Awful rooms, deserted by one of a pair of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abbreviations for king are K and R (Latin rex); removing R from PARLOURS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous means perilous or in a very bad state, a close synonym of dreadful as in 'a dreadful condition'.

clue.text: Gambler first to last? Such will misuse money

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is moved round to the end

parts.note: a speculator gambles on markets

explanation.surface: A gambler is moved from top to bottom of the list: such people waste cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the S of SPECULATOR from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculators embezzle funds entrusted to them, so they are people who misappropriate money.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about line in song

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the line

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a lyric line in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices, a traditional English choral form.

clue.text: Inactivity of party man leading country

indicators.note: leading says the partygoer comes in front of the country

parts.note: a stag is a man at a stag party, the night out before a wedding
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A political party's man heads the country while nothing happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of no movement or development, the lack of activity.

clue.text: Watercourse runs into part of camp

indicators.note: into says the runs abbreviation is placed inside the camping shelter

parts.note: a tent is one element of a campsite
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A stream flows into part of a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flowing body of water, and the Trent is a well-known English one.

clue.text: Listed as 'banned', former character initiating donations

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
late means former, as in 'the late president'

indicators.note: character initiating means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Listed as forbidden, a former figure starts making gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabulated means set out in a table, so the items are arranged in a list.

clue.text: Exhausted cricketer, first out, entering crude pavilion?

indicators.note: entering says the shortened cricketer goes inside the hut

parts.note: a shed is a rough-and-ready version of a cricket pavilion

indicators.note: first out says the opening letter of the cricketer is dropped

parts.note: a batter is a batsman

explanation.surface: A tired batsman, out first, trudges into a ramshackle pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: A pavilion is the clubhouse at a cricket ground; a shed is a crude version of one, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered is informal British for utterly worn out, a common synonym of exhausted.

clue.text: Like bits of speech from head of school, say — ridiculous

indicators.note: head of says take the leading letter of school

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
mental is slang for crazy or ridiculous

explanation.surface: A headteacher's speech, for example, is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, segmental describes the individual sound units that make up spoken language.

clue.text: Asked to protect bird having a problem walking maybe

indicators.note: to protect says the asking word wraps around the bird

parts.note: begged means asked earnestly
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded to shelter a bird that has trouble walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Legs that curve outward at the knee can give an awkward gait, hence a walking difficulty, perhaps.

clue.text: Driver of vehicle getting on in risky enterprise

indicators.note: in says the word 'on' goes inside the bet

parts.note: a wager is a bet, a risky undertaking

explanation.surface: A driver is getting on with a risky venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner is the person who drives a wagon, a horse-drawn cart.

clue.text: Player touring America — not all of it

indicators.note: not all of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer tours the United States, though not every state.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamer is someone who plays games, especially video games, so is a player.

clue.text: Staff meeting Arab ruler outside university in the capital

indicators.note: meeting says the staffing word joins up with what follows

parts.note: to man is to staff

indicators.note: outside says the ruler goes around the university

parts.note: an aga (agha) is a Turkish or Middle Eastern chief

explanation.surface: Staff meet an Arab leader outside a university in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface calls the aga Arab; strictly it is an Ottoman Turkish title.
explanation.definitionFit: Managua is the chief city and seat of government of Nicaragua, so a national capital.

clue.text: Record with old identifying symbol

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An old record carries a symbol that identifies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem used for recognition is its graphic mark, the designed badge of identity.

clue.text: Hesitation to go on holiday with bad weather? One holds back

indicators.note: to go on means the hesitation sound comes on after the rest of the pieces

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
rain is bad weather
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates about going on holiday because of bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A restrainer is a person or device that restricts or holds something in check.

clue.text: Sound and smell outside front of works

indicators.note: outside says the smell goes around the letter

parts.note: a tang is a sharp smell or taste

indicators.note: front of says take the opening letter of works

explanation.surface: A noise and an odour come from outside the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a resonant noise, like a plucked string or a nasal accent.

clue.text: Prepare to change one of the vitamins, being tall and thin

indicators.text: to change one of the vitamins
indicators.note: to change one of the vitamins says vitamin A is swapped for vitamin E in the preparing word

parts.note: to ready is to prepare

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready to alter a vitamin intake to stay lanky.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E are both vitamins: the A of READY becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy describes a person who is slender and lanky, like a reed.

clue.text: It's crazy when drug's put in alcoholic drink

indicators.note: put in says the drug is placed inside the crazy word

parts.note: mad means crazy
E is slang for the drug ecstasy; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Spiking a drink with drugs is madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is a fermented honey-based beverage containing alcohol.

clue.text: Faced with future, maybe, saint becomes most nervous

indicators.note: faced with says the grammatical form stands up against, here before, the saint

parts.note: the future is one example of a grammatical tense, hence the 'maybe'

explanation.surface: A saint, facing the future, becomes very anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means anxious or on edge, so the superlative is the most anxious.

clue.text: Feeling a glow by the fireside?

parts.note: at means by, as in 'at the door'
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Someone sits warmly by the fire, feeling a glow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one cosy scene, but 'by the fireside' is wordplay; an ingle is an old word for a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: To be atingle is to be tingling all over, a pleasant glowing sensation of excitement.

clue.text: Democrat a left-winger challenged

parts.note: a red is a communist or socialist

explanation.surface: A Democrat and a socialist square up to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Dared means challenged someone to do something risky, as in a playground taunt.

clue.text: Fabled member approaching death, casual, one drifting away

indicators.note: approaching says the limb comes up right next to the death

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member
end means death

indicators.note: drifting away says the one leaves the casual word

parts.note: airy means casual or nonchalant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A limb near its end, the casual one floats away: a tale for the ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting away' removes I from AIRY to leave ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legendary is celebrated in old stories or myths, which is what fabled means.
